headline: Vermont shelters struggle to keep up as financial hardship drives pet surrenders
dek: Rescue groups say rising care costs, housing insecurity and full facilities are making it harder to find safe homes for pets surrendered by owners in crisis.
body: Vermont animal shelters and rescue groups are seeing more requests from owners who can no longer afford or house their pets, while facilities across the state remain near capacity, VTDigger reported Sunday.

The Lucy Mackenzie Humane Society in West Windsor has seen a significant increase in surrender requests tied to financial hardship or housing insecurity, Executive Director Jackie Stanley told VTDigger. The organization, like many brick-and-mortar shelters, maintains a waiting list for new animals.

Rescue leaders and Vermont Director of Animal Welfare Lisa Milot pointed to higher veterinary and food costs, limited access to veterinary practices and landlord restrictions as overlapping pressures. For The Love of Dogs Vermont said this year has been its most intense since the group was founded in 2020, with more requests than it can accept.

VTDigger reported that one Bennington County couple contacted more than 30 shelters and rescue organizations in Vermont, New Hampshire and Maine while trying to place two dogs. The couple was repeatedly turned away because of capacity before eventually finding a shelter, illustrating how a personal financial crisis can become a statewide placement problem.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Vermont pet shelters face rising surrender requests
seoDescription: Vermont shelters and rescues report more pet surrender requests tied to financial hardship and housing insecurity while facilities remain full.
